summary: The change does exactly what the task asks: decode_base64 is wired through the existing Node-parity base64 decoder into a new go/nodeutf8 package whose WHATWG decoder I verified byte-for-byte against Node on exhaustive 2-byte and 1.5M+ 3-byte inputs, 60k longer random inputs, and 120k adversarial base64 strings (zero mismatches), plus a successful end-to-end compiled-ABAP run checking strlen; all repo suites I ran pass. The only defect is procedural: the change pushes three budgeted files/packages over their size ceilings without the required tools/osd-size-budget.json update, which the repository's own pre-push gate reports as new breaches.

findings.claim: The added lines push three budgeted targets over their ceilings with no accompanying budget update in tools/osd-size-budget.json: tools/gogen/frontend.mjs 6893 > 6890, tools/gogen/go/abap/http_utility.go 19 > 9, and go:abap 11817 > 11807. The repo's documented push gate (tools/osd-size-budget.mjs --changed origin/main, run by .githooks/pre-push, where it blocks) exits 1 on exactly these three new breaches (CI's size-budget.yml is advisory only). Additionally, once the new tools/gogen/go/nodeutf8/*.go files are committed and become tracked, the same tool flags 'go:nodeutf8: a package without a budget' (goPackages()/ownGoFiles() only count tracked files), which also needs a --update/JSON entry with a reason.
findings.repro: cd /work && node tools/osd-size-budget.mjs --changed baseline; echo exit=$?  # exit=1 with the three new breaches (baseline files sit exactly at budget: frontend.mjs 6890/6890, http_utility.go 9/9, go:abap 11807/11807)
